Read-only efficiency review completed. No files were edited, no real providers were run, and `.gold-band` was excluded.

1. **Unbounded WebSocket frame allocation before size validation**  
   `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-web\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\web\HcpWebSocketServer.java:78-83`  
   The handler allocates `new byte[message.remaining()]` and parses the protobuf before the gateway enforces its 1 MiB limit. An unauthenticated loopback peer can send one very large binary frame, causing full-frame allocation plus parser allocations before rejection and potentially exhausting heap.

2. **Every session save rebuilds complete timeline and search projections**  
   `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:218-229,463-481,536-562`  
   Each state transition deletes and reinserts every timeline and FTS row. A token, permission, or tool-state update on a 10,000-message session therefore re-encodes all messages twice, performs O(history) writes, and advances the global search revision even when searchable content is unchanged.

3. **Session mutations perform redundant full-aggregate SQLite I/O and comparisons**  
   `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\PersistentHostStore.java:47-50,229-258,270-305`  
   An update loads and decodes the full aggregate, materializes another full stored aggregate, compares up to 256 complete event payloads, saves it, then loads and decodes it again merely to return the document. Any mutation on a mature multi-megabyte session incurs redundant reads, allocations, and byte-array scans.

4. **Timeline migration blocks startup with a repository-wide rebuild**  
   `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:437-460`  
   Store construction synchronously reads and decodes every session document and rebuilds all timeline rows inside one transaction. First startup after the projection version change can remain unavailable for a long time with thousands of large sessions while holding a large write transaction.

5. **Restart harness retains unbounded process and persistent-file contents**  
   `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage4-host-restart.mjs:39-41,188-195`  
   Host stdout is appended indefinitely to one JavaScript string, and each artifact/database/WAL file is later loaded completely with `readFile`. Noisy Gradle output or a large SQLite/artifact file can grow the harness heap without bound and terminate verification before cleanup.

6. **Authentication bootstrap child can survive failed restart verification**  
   `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage4-host-restart.mjs:162-185`  
   Unlike the Host and Playwright children, the authentication child has no `finally` block that kills and awaits it. If it emits a valid frame and then hangs, or errors before completing the frame, `authenticate` rejects while the process and pipes may remain alive; a frame already read before `processExit` times out also bypasses the buffer-zeroing block.
**Verifying candidate filtering to weird agent ID**

1. `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-web\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\web\HcpWebSocketServer.java:78-83` — The inbound HCP limit is checked only after allocating, copying, and parsing the complete WebSocket frame. A loopback peer can send an arbitrarily large pre-authentication frame, causing heap exhaustion before the 1 MiB gateway limit rejects it.

2. `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:218-229,463-481,536-562` — Every session save deletes and recreates the complete timeline and FTS projection. A minor transition on a 10,000-message session re-encodes and writes every message and invalidates all search cursors even when searchable content is unchanged.

3. `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\PersistentHostStore.java:47-50,229-258,270-305` — Each mutation loads and decodes the full aggregate, materializes and deeply compares it—including up to 256 snapshot payloads—saves it, then reloads it just to return the document. Mature multi-megabyte sessions therefore incur redundant full SQLite I/O on hot transitions.

4. `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:437-460` — Store construction synchronously reads and decodes every session document and rebuilds all timeline rows in one transaction. First startup after migration with many large sessions blocks Host readiness and holds a repository-wide write transaction.

5. `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage4-host-restart.mjs:39-41,188-195` — The restart harness accumulates all Host stdout in an unbounded string and reads each artifact, database, and WAL file completely into memory. Noisy Gradle output or one large persistence file can exhaust the Node heap before cleanup.

6. `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage4-host-restart.mjs:162-185` — The authentication bootstrap lacks the child termination and wait cleanup used for Host and Playwright. If it emits a frame and hangs, or errors before completing a frame, verification throws while the process and pipes can remain alive; a frame read before exit timeout can also bypass zeroing.
